findings.title: Input manifest digest is only format-checked
findings.observed: The resolver requires the exact inputManifest filename and merely checks inputManifestSha256 against the 64-lowercase-hex pattern. A hermetic admission with inputManifestSha256 set to 64 zeros still returned the governed CRM-307 binding when the exact body was present.
findings.impact: The adoption record can carry a false provenance digest while still being accepted. The current root input manifest is tracked and hashes to 60de802c3e193b4d205018fe960f197e972cae2eba1f6f935d680b38da3ce844, so the resolver can verify the named file and exact digest instead of treating the field as decorative metadata.
findings.requiredFix: Resolve the fixed tracked input-manifest path under the repository root, reject symlink or escape paths as appropriate, and require its current SHA-256 to equal admission.inputManifestSha256. Add a hermetic mutation test that changes the digest and expects null.

findings.title: Conflicting acquired receipt candidate is ignored
findings.observed: The resolver filters for matching acquired receipts and requires one match, but it does not reject an additional acquired receipt for the same recovery source with a different digest. A fixture containing the current correct acquired receipt plus a second acquired receipt with an all-zero SHA still returned the governed binding.
findings.impact: Ambiguous source custody is silently accepted when one candidate happens to match the hard-coded pin. That leaves the governed adoption record with contradictory acquired evidence.
findings.requiredFix: Count all acquired receipt candidates for the exact recovery source, require exactly one acquired candidate, and require that candidate to match the immutable source ID, SHA, length and filename. Add a duplicate-conflicting-receipt refusal test.

findings.title: Unresolved custody row with conflicting heldAs is overridden
findings.observed: The CA custody conflict filter only tests source.resolved === true. A hermetic CA row with the expected source ID, resolved false, and a non-null heldAs pointing to wrong.pdf was treated as the ordinary stale zero-source shape; the resolver appended the governed path and familySources returned the correct path with no unresolvable entry.
findings.impact: A conflicting custody assertion can be hidden by the bridge simply because its resolved flag is false. The exact governed path does not control the row when a non-null alternate binding is present.
findings.requiredFix: Permit the known stale shape only when heldAs is absent; if the expected CA source ID has any non-null heldAs or a resolved binding, require exact path, SHA and byte length, otherwise add an unresolvable conflict and block family_sources_bind. Add a negative test for resolved false with conflicting heldAs.

findings.title: Transferred full test file is stale against the current closed Kansas families
findings.observed: The full supplied test file ran 16 tests with 15 passed and 1 failed. The unchanged assertion expects ks-22-2410-arrest-set to be UNRESOLVABLE, but current Captain custody already has three exact resolved sources and the current family_sources_bind result is BINDS. The second registration-relief assertion is likewise a current closed exact-source family and is not a valid negative fixture.

currentEvidence.failure: Expected UNRESOLVABLE; actual BINDS for ks-22-2410-arrest-set

findings.impact: The focused regression suite is not green on the current Captain, so a claimed passing patch review would conceal an environment-dependent stale negative assertion.
findings.requiredFix: Replace this current-state negative with a hermetic synthetic missing-indexed-body fixture or narrow it to a demonstrably absent source. Preserve the existing missing/corrupt-body and ambiguity refusals, and do not turn it into a queue-pin-only check.
findings.implementationCausality: The CA-specific additions did not alter Kansas resolution; this is a pre-existing assertion that predates the current Kansas closures. It still blocks a green current-Captain review.
